---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`). Before working on a graph node,
  inspect its tags and any `TO CHECK` reason; `TO CHECK` is an attention marker,
  not a mathematical verdict.
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space).     32	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) where
    33	  hom : pullback T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X
    34	  commutes : hom ≫ f =
    35	    pullback.snd T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))

   107	theorem overHomEquiv_precomp (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
   108	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)

     8	/-!
     9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
    10	
    11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
    12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
    13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
    14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
    15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
    16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
    17	
    18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
    19	
    20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
    21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
    22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
    23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
    24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
    25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
    26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
    27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
    28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
    29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
    30	
    31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
    32	
    33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
    34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
    35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
    36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
    37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
    38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
    39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
    40	
    41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
    42	
    43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
    44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
    45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
    46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
    47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
    48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
    49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
    50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
    51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
    52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
    53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
    54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
    55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
    56	
    57	## Main declarations
    58	
    59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
    61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
    62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
    63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
    64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
    65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
    66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.
    67	-/

    74	open CategoryTheory Opposite
    75	
    76	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    77	
    78	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    79	
    80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
    81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
    82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
    83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
    84	
    85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
    86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
    87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    89	    Type (u + 1) where
    90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
    91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
    92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
    93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
    94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the
    95	  EGA limit criterion. -/
    96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
    97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
    98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
    99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/
   100	  quasiCompact : QuasiCompact J.hom
   101	
   102	namespace JacobianData
   103	
   104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   106	
   107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
   108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
   109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
   110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
   111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
   112	@[implicit_reducible]
   113	noncomputable def grpObj (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj d.J :=
   114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
   115	
   116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
   117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
   118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
   119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
   120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
   121	  d.rep.homEquiv
   122	
   123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
   124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
   125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
   126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
   128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
   129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
   130	
   131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
   132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
   133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
   134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
   135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
   136	
   137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
   138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
   139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
   141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
   142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
   143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
   144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
   145	
   146	end JacobianData

     9	/-!
    10	# A finite affine atlas for the separably closed Picard representer
    11	
    12	The exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer is quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and
    13	locally of finite presentation over the ground field.  This file combines those facts
    14	into a finite affine atlas whose overlap spaces are quasi-compact and whose chart rings
    15	are finitely presented over the ground field.  This is the finite collection of algebraic
    16	data needed to spread the representer out from a separable closure.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false

    21	universe u

    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-! ## A project-local finite-cover supplement -/
    30	
    31	/-- A quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme has a finite affine open cover with
    32	quasi-compact pairwise intersections. -/
    33	theorem Scheme.exists_finite_affineCover_inter_isQuasiCompact (X : Scheme.{u})
    34	    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    35	    ∃ s : Set X.affineOpens, s.Finite ∧ (⨆ i ∈ s, (i : X.Opens)) = ⊤ ∧
    36	      ∀ U ∈ s, ∀ V ∈ s, IsCompact ((U : Set X) ∩ (V : Set X)) := by
    37	  obtain ⟨s, hs, he⟩ :=
    38	    (isCompact_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens (U := (⊤ : X.Opens))).mp
    39	      (by simpa using isCompact_univ (X := X))
    40	  refine ⟨s, hs, he.symm, ?_⟩
    41	  intro U _ V _
    42	  exact quasiSeparatedSpace_iff_forall_affineOpens.mp ‹_› U V
    43	
    44	/-- A finite affine presentation of the intersection of two affine opens.  Besides
    45	covering the intersection exactly, it records finite presentation of both restriction
    46	maps from the chart rings to every overlap-piece ring. -/
    47	structure Scheme.FiniteAffineOverlapPresentation (X : Scheme.{u})
    48	    (U V : X.affineOpens) where
    49	  pieces : Set X.affineOpens
    50	  finite_pieces : pieces.Finite
    51	  iSup_opens : (⨆ W ∈ pieces, (W : X.Opens)) = U.1 ⊓ V.1
    52	  piece_le_left : ∀ W ∈ pieces, W.1 ≤ U.1
    53	  piece_le_right : ∀ W ∈ pieces, W.1 ≤ V.1
    54	  leftRestriction_finitePresentation : ∀ W (hW : W ∈ pieces),
    55	    (X.homOfLE (piece_le_left W hW)).appTop.hom.FinitePresentation
    56	  rightRestriction_finitePresentation : ∀ W (hW : W ∈ pieces),
    57	    (X.homOfLE (piece_le_right W hW)).appTop.hom.FinitePresentation
    58	
    59	/-- A compact intersection of two affine opens admits a finite affine overlap
    60	presentation.  The two restriction maps are finitely presented because the inclusions
    61	of the affine overlap pieces into the affine charts are open immersions. -/
    62	noncomputable def Scheme.finiteAffineOverlapPresentation (X : Scheme.{u})
    63	    (U V : X.affineOpens) (h : IsCompact ((U : Set X) ∩ (V : Set X))) :
    64	    X.FiniteAffineOverlapPresentation U V := by
    65	  apply Classical.choice
    66	  obtain ⟨s, hs, he⟩ :=
    67	    (isCompact_iff_finite_and_eq_biUnion_affineOpens (U := U.1 ⊓ V.1)).mp
    68	      (by simpa using h)
    69	  have hle (W : X.affineOpens) (hW : W ∈ s) : W.1 ≤ U.1 ⊓ V.1 := by
    70	    rw [he]
    71	    exact le_iSup_of_le W (le_iSup_of_le hW le_rfl)
    72	  refine ⟨
    73	    { pieces := s
    74	      finite_pieces := hs
    75	      iSup_opens := he.symm
    76	      piece_le_left := fun W hW => (hle W hW).trans inf_le_left
    77	      piece_le_right := fun W hW => (hle W hW).trans inf_le_right
    78	      leftRestriction_finitePresentation := ?_
    79	      rightRestriction_finitePresentation := ?_ }⟩
    80	  · intro W hW
    81	    exact (X.homOfLE ((hle W hW).trans inf_le_left)).finitePresentation_appTop
    82	  · intro W hW
    83	    exact (X.homOfLE ((hle W hW).trans inf_le_right)).finitePresentation_appTop

    85	/-! ## The finite atlas on the exact `Pic^0` representer -/

    87	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    88	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    89	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    90	
    91	/-- A finite affine atlas on the exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer, including
    92	the two finiteness properties needed for chart-ring spreading: quasi-compact overlaps
    93	and finite presentation of every selected chart ring over the ground field. -/

    95	  charts : Set (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.affineOpens
    96	  finite_charts : charts.Finite
    97	  iSup_opens :
    98	    (⨆ U ∈ charts,

   103	        (V : Set (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left))
   104	  chartRing_finitePresentation : ∀ U ∈ charts,
   105	    ((pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.hom.appLE
   106	      (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) U.1 le_top).hom.FinitePresentation

   110	/-- The finite affine atlas obtained from quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, and
   111	local finite presentation of the exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer. -/

   113	  apply Classical.choice
   114	  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
   115	  letI : QuasiCompact J.hom := quasiCompact_pic0SepClosedRepresenter C
   116	  letI : CompactSpace J.left := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace J.hom

   118	  letI : LocallyOfFinitePresentation J.hom :=
   119	    locallyOfFinitePresentation_pic0_sepClosed_representableBy C

   137	def Pic0FiniteStageChartRing
   138	    (U : { U // U ∈ (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).charts }) : Type u :=

   153	algebra structure over the separably closed ground field. -/

   155	    (U : { U // U ∈ (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).charts }) :

    10	/-!
    11	# Affine intersections in the finite-stage Picard atlas
    12	
    13	The exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer is a group scheme over a field, hence is
    14	separated.  Consequently the intersection of any two affine charts in its chosen finite
    15	atlas is itself affine.  The canonical affine overlap packaged here is the geometric input
    16	for spreading out the finite atlas's restriction maps and gluing data.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	/-- The finite index type of charts in the chosen atlas of the exact separably closed
    34	`Pic^0` representer. -/
    35	abbrev Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex :=
    36	  { U // U ∈ (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).charts }
    37	
    38	instance : Finite (Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :=
    39	  (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).finite_charts.to_subtype
    40	
    41	/-- Pairwise intersections of charts in the chosen finite atlas of the exact separably
    42	closed `Pic^0` representer are affine.  This uses the group structure transported from
    43	the represented Picard functor, rather than adding separatedness as a hypothesis. -/
    44	theorem pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine
    45	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    46	    IsAffineOpen (U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1) := by
    47	  let J := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1
    48	  letI : GrpObj J := (picRepDatumSepClosed C).grpObj
    49	  haveI : IsSeparated J.hom := isSeparated_of_grpObj J
    50	  haveI : Scheme.IsSeparated J.left := by
    51	    constructor
    52	    rw [← Limits.terminal.comp_from J.hom]
    53	    infer_instance
    54	  exact U.1.2.inf V.1.2
    55	
    56	/-- The intersection of two chosen finite-stage charts, regarded canonically as an affine
    57	open of the exact separably closed `Pic^0` representer. -/
    58	noncomputable def pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap
    59	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    60	    (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.affineOpens :=
    61	  ⟨U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1, pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine C U V⟩
    62	
    63	@[simp]
    64	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_open
    65	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    66	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 = U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1 :=
    67	  rfl
    68	
    69	/-- The canonical affine overlap is contained in its left chart. -/
    70	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_left
    71	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    72	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 ≤ U.1.1 :=
    73	  inf_le_left
    74	
    75	/-- The canonical affine overlap is contained in its right chart. -/
    76	theorem pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap_le_right
    77	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    78	    (pic0FiniteStageAffineOverlap C U V).1 ≤ V.1.1 :=
    79	  inf_le_right
    80	
    81	/-! ## The canonical finite affine gluing datum -/
    82	
    83	/-- The chosen finite atlas as an actual open cover of the exact separably closed `Pic^0`
    84	representer. -/
    85	noncomputable def pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover :
    86	    (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.OpenCover :=
    87	  (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1.left.openCoverOfIsOpenCover
    88	    (fun U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C => U.1.1) (by
    89	      apply TopologicalSpace.IsOpenCover.mk
    90	      rw [iSup_subtype'']
    91	      exact (pic0FiniteStageAtlas C).iSup_opens)
    92	
    93	/-- Every object of the chosen finite open cover is affine. -/
    94	instance pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover_isAffine (U : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
    95	    IsAffine ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).X U) := by
    96	  change IsAffine U.1.1.toScheme
    97	  exact U.1.2
    98	
    99	/-- The canonical finite affine gluing datum associated by Mathlib to the chosen open cover.
   100	Its transition maps and triple-overlap cocycle are construction output of `gluedCover`; this
   101	does not yet assert that the datum descends to a finite subextension. -/
   102	noncomputable def pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData : Scheme.GlueData :=
   103	  (pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).gluedCover
   104	
   105	/-- Every pairwise overlap scheme in the canonical finite gluing datum is affine. -/
   106	instance isAffine_pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData_V
   107	    (U V : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C) :
   108	    IsAffine ((pic0SepClosedAtlasGlueData C).V (U, V)) := by
   109	  letI : IsAffine (U.1.1 ⊓ V.1.1).toScheme :=
   110	    pic0FiniteStageAtlas_inter_isAffine C U V
   111	  let h := isPullback_opens_inf U.1.1 V.1.1
   112	  change IsAffine
   113	    (pullback ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).f U)
   114	      ((pic0SepClosedAtlasOpenCover C).f V))
   115	  change IsAffine (pullback U.1.1.ι V.1.1.ι)
   116	  exact IsAffine.of_isIso h.isoPullback.inv
   117	
   118	end

   120	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The descent assembly — the theorem that CONSUMES the four repair inputs
    12	
    13	`AJC.picrep.etale-rep.descent-assembly`.
    14	
    15	## Why this file exists
    16	
    17	The repaired route to the seam `sorry` `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`
    18	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) is documented at that declaration as
    19	having **four inputs**, and each of the four has either landed or is held by a
    20	lane. What no declaration in this project stated is the theorem those four are
    21	inputs *to*: the step that takes a representation over a larger field and
    22	returns one over `k`.
    23	
    24	Measured before this file was written, at HEAD with fresh oleans: the seam's
    25	conclusion shape `Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X)` occurs at
    26	exactly three sites — `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` twice (the
    27	`HasPicSchemeEt` class field, and the `sorry`-bodied seam itself) and
    28	`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` once
    29	(`hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability`). All three are **same-field**:
    30	the last takes a `picSharp` representation over the *same* `k` and transports it
    31	along subcanonicity. None takes a `k'`-side representation and concludes over
    32	`k`. Independently re-measured by `review-ajc` (`I-1256`) before this file
    33	landed.
    34	
    35	So the route's scoreboard was a list of antecedents with no goal attached, and an
    36	input nobody held would have stayed invisible — the failure mode this file is
    37	written to remove.
    38	
    39	## What is proved here, and what is not
    40	
    41	**Proved, `sorry`-free** (§2): the **uniqueness half** of the descent, at the
    42	cover the repair uses. `picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest` says restriction along
    43	the single morphism `T ×_k k' ⟶ T` is *injective* on `picEt`-classes, for every
    44	`k`-test `T`. This is what makes a descended class unique once it exists.
    45	
    46	**Proved, `sorry`-free** (§3): the transport that makes the `k'`-side hypothesis
    47	statable in the right variables (`representableByRestrict_of_baseChange`, free from
    48	input 2). The other half of the class-level descent — a compatible family has a
    49	unique amalgamation — is `Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve`
    50	(`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`), cited in §3 rather than restated.
    51	
    52	**Not proved, and named rather than hidden** (§4): `G1` invariance — producing the
    53	compatible family from a Galois-invariant `k'`-class — and then the `G2` quotient
    54	construction that turns descended classes into a representing `k`-scheme, gated on
    55	`AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient` (affine half only). Neither is
    56	sheaf-theoretic; this file does not weaken either, does not restate them more
    57	cheaply, and does not close them.
    58	
    59	**What this file deliberately does not contain.** An earlier draft stated the
    60	assembly as a Lean implication whose antecedent was the seam's clause (1) and whose
    61	conclusion was the same existential — i.e. `P → P`, the shape `I-0838` forbids and
    62	the 2026-07-29 audit found 67 times. It was removed before committing rather than
    63	dressed up: the remaining obligation is a *construction*, so its home is the gate
    64	in `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`, not a hypothesis slot here. Nor is any
    65	conclusion in this file class-valued: because `instHasPicSchemeEt` is
    66	unconditional, instance search discharges a `HasPicSchemeEt`-valued conclusion by
    67	projecting the seam `sorry` for every object in the gate's domain, so such a
    68	statement would typecheck whatever its hypotheses said (`review-ajc`, `I-1251`).
    69	
    70	## What this does NOT do
    71	
    72	It closes no `sorry` in `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` and witnesses no
    73	antecedent of `fgaPicardRepresentability` for any curve. §2 is a genuine theorem
    74	about `picEt` on an arbitrary smooth proper curve over an arbitrary field, with no
    75	hypothesis on `C(k)` per `I-0491`; the statements of §3 are unconditional, and what
    76	§4 records as remaining has no producer.
    77	
    78	## A route correction recorded here because it was nearly acted on
    79	
    80	`review-ajc` proposed (and, once shown this, withdrew — `I-1256`) that the
    81	assembly should conclude the `picSharp`-shaped endpoint
    82	`∃ X, Nonempty ((picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧
    83	IsSeparated X.hom`, on the strength of its own r5 measurement that this single
    84	existential discharges *both* seam conjuncts with nothing left over. That
    85	reduction is correct and is cited below at the **input** end. As a *conclusion*
    86	over the headline's arbitrary `k` it is inadmissible, and this project already
    87	proves why: `PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
    88	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) says no scheme at all represents `picSharp C`
    89	over such a `k` once `picEtComparison C` fails to be an isomorphism. Aiming the
    90	assembly there would have produced a green, `sorry`-free theorem refutable from a
    91	lemma two files away. The whole content of the repair is that the object crossing
    92	the descent step is `picEt`.
    93	
    94	## Measurement discipline
    95	
    96	`lake build AlgebraicJacobian` EXIT=0 (8869 jobs) with **fresh** oleans before
    97	every probe below — a stale-import environment reports every probe as succeeding
    98	(`I-1057`), which would have made the §2 proof look free when it was not.

   101	universe u
   102	
   103	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry Limits
   104	
   105	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   106	
   107	namespace Scheme
   108	
   109	namespace PicScheme
   110	
   111	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {k' : Type u} [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
   112	
   113	/-! ## §1. The cover of a `k`-test by its base change, as an `Over`-morphism -/
   114	
   115	/-- The base change `T ×_k Spec k'` of a `k`-test `T`, regarded as a `k'`-test
   116	via the second projection.
   117	
   118	This is the object the descent step's classes live on: a class over `k'` is a
   119	class on `T_{k'}` for the tests `T` of interest, and `§2` shows a `k`-class is
   120	determined by its restriction here. -/
   121	noncomputable abbrev baseTest (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
   122	    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k')) :=
   123	  Over.mk (pullback.snd T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
   124	
   125	/-- **The covering morphism `T_{k'} ⟶ T`**, in the slice over `Spec k`.
   126	
   127	Its underlying scheme map is exactly `pullback.fst`, which is the morphism
   128	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` builds its covering sieve from — so the sheaf
   129	axiom landed there applies to this morphism on the nose (checked by `rfl`:
   130	`coverMap_left`). -/
   131	noncomputable def coverMap (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
   132	    (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T) ⟶ T :=
   133	  Over.homMk (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))
   134	    (pullback.condition (f := T.hom) (g := specMapAlgebra k k'))
   135	
   136	/-- The cover morphism's underlying scheme map **is** `pullback.fst`, definitionally.
   137	
   138	This is the identification that lets `§2` feed
   139	`Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees`, whose sieve is generated by
   140	`Presieve.singleton (pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k'))`. -/
   141	@[simp]
   142	theorem coverMap_left (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) :
   143	    (coverMap (k' := k') T).left = pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k') := rfl
   144	
   145	/-! ## §2. The uniqueness half of the descent — PROVED -/
   146	
   147	/-- **Restriction along `T_{k'} ⟶ T` is injective on `picEt`-classes.**
   148	
   149	For a smooth proper curve `C` over an arbitrary field `k`, an arbitrary finite
   150	separable `k'/k`, and an arbitrary `k`-test `T`: two classes in
   151	`Pic_{(C/k)ét}(T)` that agree after restriction to `T ×_k Spec k'` are equal.
   152	
   153	This is the *uniqueness* half of the descent step, and it is what makes a
   154	descended class unique once one exists — so a consumer holding a single class,
   155	rather than a compatible family, needs no separate uniqueness hypothesis.
   156	
   157	**Where the content is, stated precisely.** The amalgamation property itself is
   158	free: `Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_of_mem` holds at *every* covering sieve of
   159	`etaleTopologyOver k`, `⊤` included, because it is `PicSharp.etaleSheaf`'s own
   160	`Sheaf.cond` pushed through the forgetful functor. What this lemma adds over
   161	`Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees` is the reduction from that lemma's
   162	*sieve-indexed* hypothesis — agreement after restriction along **every** arrow of
   163	the generated sieve — to agreement along the **single** morphism `coverMap`. The
   164	step is the factorisation: an arrow of the sieve factors through `pullback.fst`,
   165	and lifting that factorisation to the slice over `Spec k` is where
   166	`pullback.condition` is consumed.
   167	
   168	**That the factorisation is not avoidable is measured, not assumed** — it is the
   169	obvious refutation of this lemma ("the sheaf axiom gives injectivity directly, so
   170	the hand proof is redundant"), so it was probed rather than argued. Two routes,
   171	both `EXIT=1`:
   172	
   173	* deriving it from the amalgamation statement
   174	  (`Scheme.isSheafFor_picEt_pullback_presieve`) requires exhibiting a
   175	  `Presieve.FamilyOfElements` on the *whole* sieve for which both classes are
   176	  amalgamations, and constructing that family needs a value at every sieve arrow —
   177	  i.e. the same factorisation, relocated;
   178	* discharging the sieve-indexed goal from the single-morphism hypothesis with no
   179	  factorisation work fails: `exact h`, `simpa using h`, `congrArg _ h` and `aesop`
   180	  all leave the goal open (`aesop` reports exhaustive search).
   181	
   182	So the content is the reduction, and only the reduction. Whoever re-checks this
   183	should re-run those two probes rather than trust the paragraph.
   184	
   185	**No hypothesis on `C(k)`** (`I-0491`), and none on `T`. The finite-separability
   186	binders are inherited from the covering-sieve membership witness of
   187	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean`, which is where they are genuinely used; they are
   188	*not* needed by the cross-base identification (`picEt_crossBaseIso` holds for an
   189	arbitrary field extension). -/
   190	theorem picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest
   191	    [FiniteDimensional k k'] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k']
   192	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   193	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   194	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   195	    {t₁ t₂ : (picEt C).obj (Opposite.op T)}
   196	    (h : (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t₁
   197	       = (picEt C).map (coverMap (k' := k') T).op t₂) :
   198	    t₁ = t₂ := by
   199	  refine AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees k' C T ?_
   200	  intro W g hg
   201	  rw [Sieve.overEquiv_symm_iff] at hg
   202	  obtain ⟨Z, a, b, hb, hfac⟩ := hg
   203	  cases hb
   204	  -- `g` factors through `coverMap` in the slice over `Spec k`.
   205	  have hgfac : g = (Over.homMk a (by
   206	      rw [← Over.w g]
   207	      simp only [restrictTest, Over.map_obj_hom, baseTest, Over.mk_hom, ← hfac]
   208	      rw [Category.assoc]
   209	      exact congrArg (a ≫ ·) pullback.condition.symm) :
   210	        W ⟶ (restrictTest k k').obj (baseTest (k' := k') T))
   211	      ≫ coverMap (k' := k') T := by
   212	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   213	    change Over.Hom.left g = a ≫ pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k')
   214	    exact hfac.symm
   215	  rw [hgfac]
   216	  simp only [op_comp, Functor.map_comp, CategoryTheory.comp_apply, h]
   217	
   218	/-! ## §3. The input-side transport, and the sharp form of what remains -/
   219	
   220	/-- **The `k'`-side input, transported: PROVED, and free.**
   221	
   222	A representation of `picEt` of the **base-changed curve** `C_{k'}` by a
   223	`k'`-scheme `X'` is the same thing as a representation of `picEt C` restricted to
   224	`k'`-tests. This is `picEt_crossBaseIso` (input 2 of the repair, closed
   225	unconditionally by `Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean`) fed to
   226	`Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`.
   227	
   228	It is recorded because it is the step that makes the assembly's hypothesis
   229	*statable in the right variables*: without it the `k'`-scheme that campaign `J5`
